blocker_fixes.method: 17 counterexample tests written first and confirmed failing on the previous implementation (1 pre-existing guard test already passed); after the fix, mutation checks removed each guard (creation-time attribution, root identity abort, forget gating under a busy lock) and confirmed its test fails
blocker_fixes.A_attribution: _win_terminate_tree opens every candidate once before signalling anything; each target's creation time must be strictly after its verified parent's and no later than the snapshot completion time; the root instance's creation must match the trusted anchor (mismatch aborts the whole stop); termination and waiting use the same pinned handle. A completely dead root cannot bound its children's creation window, so candidates are reported and never signalled. Documented boundary: grandchildren of a middle process that died before it could be opened are invisible (missed cleanup, never a misattributed kill).
blocker_fixes.B_failure_reporting: INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE rejected; Process32First/Next distinguish ERROR_NO_MORE_FILES from enumeration failure (partial table aborts the stop); OpenProcess separates gone/access-denied/other; TerminateProcess and wait results checked; one shared monotonic deadline for the whole tree; every handle closed; cleanup_child and stop_owned raise with retained identities and keep the PID record whenever an exit is unconfirmed
blocker_fixes.C_record_hygiene: process reclamation and shared-record mutation are separated; without the control lock cleanup_children passes forget=False so a stale cleanup can never unlink a concurrent launcher's replacement record
blocker_fixes.tests: python/tests/test_process_tree.py: 18 tests (fake-API attribution/failure matrix + real Windows processes: full-tree stop, bystander survival, dead-root candidates retained)
